column1: # params.tsv -- every threshold in the pipeline, with its provenance.
# This file exists because of CLAUDE.md rule 1: "a plausible-looking number is
# not a number. If a threshold is a guess, it is labelled a guess in the
# parameter block's metadata and it is on chunk 8's tuning list." Until this
# file existed the thresholds were Rust constants and there was nowhere to
# write that label, so the labels lived in doc comments where no report could
# read them. Now a build can print exactly which numbers in the engine are
# guesses, and a benchmark run can say which of them it moved.
#   name        dotted path: stage.parameter. The identity the `params` table
#               and `ocrcer_core::params` both key on. Never renamed in place.
#   provenance  measured  -- read off a run that is named in `note`
#               authored  -- follows from a stated principle, not a sweep
#               guess     -- a plausible starting value and nothing more
#   tune        yes if chunk 8 should sweep it, no if sweeping it is
#               meaningless (a definition rather than a threshold)
#   note        one line: where the number came from, or what would change it
# The Rust side carries the same defaults as constants so the engine runs
# without a model file at all. That is a duplication, and it is made safe by
# `ocrcer-build`'s `params` test, which fails the day the two disagree --
# CLAUDE.md rule 4's requirement is that nothing silently diverges, not that
# a default may never appear twice.

column6: note
ARCHITECTURE.md section 6; Sauvola's own recommended neighbourhood for text of ordinary size
ARCHITECTURE.md section 6; mid-range Sauvola k, biased slightly toward keeping thin strokes
half of an 8-bit range: the dynamic-range normaliser in Sauvola, a definition rather than a threshold
tan 5 degrees, which is the sweep ARCHITECTURE.md section 6 specifies
below this a shear moves no pixel on a page of ordinary width, so correcting costs a resample and buys nothing
a single pixel is speckle; two is the smallest mark that could be ink
half: an x-height letter beside a capital on the same baseline clears this, and a letter on the next line does not
a component taller than a fifth of the page is a rule, a border or a frame rather than a character

a component whose longer ink extent exceeds this multiple of its shorter one is not a glyph; 0 disables the gate, and it ships disabled because every value tried made things worse. The intent was a scale-free companion to furniture_fraction, which is measured against the whole page and so cannot see a rule drawn inside one cell of a form. The bound a value must clear was measured first: `ocrcer-build aspect` renders all 187 charset classes on all 19 shippable faces at 256 px/em and the flattest is the em dash on Open Sans Condensed Light at 236x10 px = 23.60:1 (next flat class `_` 12.83:1; the extreme in the other orientation is the bar at 12x256 = 21.33:1). Measured on 29 hand-checked scans at lines.column_gap_heights=1.5, word F1 fell monotonically as the gate tightened: off 22.626%, 28 22.473%, 16 22.213%, 10 21.860%, and precision with it (15.134 / 14.988 / 14.758 / 14.500). On the 625-page synthetic corpus 28 is inert to every digit. The mechanism by which removing components lowers precision is not understood, and the measurement was taken before words.min_valley_x_heights existed, so it is worth re-running; until it is, 0 is the value with the evidence
a dot or an accent is much shorter than the letters it belongs to; a third is the band that separates them
how far above its host a mark may float before it is a line of its own
how far below the baseline ink must reach to count as a descender rather than as a baseline wobble
how far a component may hang below a band and still be its descender rather than a line of its own; a comma on a line with no other descender is the case
median over the 19 shippable faces, `ocrcer-build metrics`, 2026-09-22; min 0.6335, max 0.8051

the plausibility floor on XHeightSource::Observed: main must be at least this fraction of cap, or the branch that would call it Observed falls through as if upper were empty. A band formed by two lines merging (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23, "Merged lines: split on two baselines") produces a tops histogram piled at zero -- every member of the wrongly-absorbed second line clamps to top == 0 against the first line's baseline -- so main comes back as the clamp floor of 1 rather than a real measurement, while upper still holds the first line's genuine x-height and cap-height values and so is non-empty; !upper.is_empty() alone cannot tell that pathology from an ordinary condensed face, so this checks the one thing that does. Half of the smallest per-face x-height/cap-height ratio across the shippable font set, `ocrcer-build metrics` (2026-09-23, 32 faces): the extreme is 0.6335 (OCRcer Technical, deliberately large-on-the-body), so the floor is 0.3168, a full factor of two of headroom below the most condensed real face this engine ships. The traced defect (`docs/measurements/2026-09-23_line_merge_mechanism.md`) measured about 0.08 -- clear of even a floor this conservative. See `docs/measurements/2026-09-23_line_merge_phase2.txt`

a line whose x-height came out below this fraction of the page's typical x-height did not measure one and takes the page's instead. The case is a line with no x-height evidence of its own -- a row of leader dots, a row of underscores, a rule -- whose members are all one small height, so its modal band is punctuation and every glyph on it is then measured against a ruler a fifth of the right length. A guess, and it is a guess about a gap rather than about a boundary: real same-page size variation is footnotes at about 0.8 of body text and fine print at about 0.7, while a leader line measures 0.2 to 0.3, so anything from 0.4 to 0.6 separates them. Not swept; on the tuning list

a horizontal gap between consecutive components of a line wider than this many median component heights is a column or box boundary and the line is cut there. Line banding is purely horizontal, so on a ruled form a 6 pt field label and a 14 pt display heading three boxes away land in one line with one x-height, which is wrong for both: the word splitter then over-splits the large text and under-splits the small text on the same line. The populations were measured over 384 uncut lines of bench/pages-cov, classified by the word splitter's own per-line threshold: an intra-word gap is 0.14 median heights at the median and 0.30 at p90, a word space is 0.57 at the median, 1.25 at p90 and tops out at 1.64 on running text, and the widest gap inside one banded row is 3.25 median on invoice and 5.30 on statement with a tail past 20. That supersedes the asserted figures that stood here, which named the intra-word gap (0.2) as the word space and the running-text ceiling (1.5) as the tabbed column gap; both understated the separation. Decided at 1.75 from a sweep of both word F1 and CER on bench/pages-cov (625 pages) and finfilings (60 pages): both agree the cut beats cut-off on both corpora, and 1.75 sits on the plateau around the 1.5 peak with a quarter-step more margin from its cliff than 1.5 itself, while finfilings cannot tell 1.75 from 2.5. See `docs/measurements/2026-09-22_column_gap_sweep_final.txt` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-22 ("lines.column_gap_heights is decided at 1.75"). 0 disables the cut

whether a column_gap_heights candidate between two single-component fragments -- a leader dot beside another leader dot -- is dropped (1) rather than cut (0, the plain greedy cut, byte-identical to cutting at every candidate). Both readings have now cost real pages: the narrowed rule reasoned from the leader fixture measured `bench/pages-cov` F1 76.675%/CER 6.503% (identical to control) but `finfilings` F1 67.865% against a 68.277% control (-0.41, over the 0.2 gate) and CER 19.610% against 19.544% (docs/measurements/2026-09-23_column_fragment_min.txt). Ships 0, the configuration both corpora measured best; the toggle exists so both behaviours run from one binary for a per-page diff before a third rule is reasoned. `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23 ("The narrowed lone-glyph rule also fails the real-filings gate"). Not a threshold to sweep

whether the two-baseline split post-pass runs: 0 leaves band growth's output untouched, 1 runs the split on every band before measure(). Measured 2026-09-23 with lines.x_height_floor_per_cap in place: finfilings CER 19.007 -> 17.064, F1 72.818 -> 73.615; pages-cov unchanged (F1 77.392, CER 6.127). A real text line has exactly one baseline; a band two lines were merged into (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23, "Merged lines: split on two baselines") has two, well separated and each with its own support -- the same asymmetry lines.x_height_floor_per_cap exploits from the other side. Ships 0 until measured against both corpora, per the chunk-8 tuning list. See `docs/measurements/2026-09-23_line_merge_phase2.txt`

how far apart two baseline peaks must sit, as a fraction of the band's median body height, before the fainter one is treated as a second line rather than baseline wobble on one line. A guess, on the chunk-8 list

the least support the fainter baseline peak may carry, as a fraction of the dominant peak's support, and the most weight the valley between them may carry, as a fraction of the fainter peak's support; both read off the same number. A guess, on the chunk-8 list

how many bins on either side of each baseline peak the valley sum skips, as a fraction of the band's median body height; 0.0 keeps the historical fixed two-bin margin. `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23 ("Line fusion fix"): a fixed two-bin margin does not scale with type size, so on real prose at this corpus's body size a peak's own descenders (g p q y j) reach several pixels past it -- more than two bins -- and their weight then counts as valley evidence of a third baseline instead of being recognised as the peak's own ink; a neighbouring peak's own leading edge (round-bottomed letters landing a couple of raster rows above the modal baseline) shows the mirror case just short of that peak. Diagnosed directly on filing__r000308's three largest fused bands (`OCRCER_DEBUG_SPLIT`-gated instrumentation, removed): every one of the three failed the valley test, and each failure decomposed exactly into one or both of those two populations and nothing else -- e.g. body=232 median_body=14 i1_y=70 i2_y=92 valley=536 (needed<=416.2) resolved fully into i1's own descender tail at y1=72..76 (115+22+108+194+97=536, offsets +2..+6 bins from i1); a second band's valley=778 (needed<=353.5) resolved into that same i1-tail pattern (392) plus a cluster at y1=136, two bins short of i2=138 (386). Measured 2026-09-23: a two-page screen (r000308, r000363) found 0.3 best among {0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.7}; the full-corpus run at 0.3 gave finfilings end-to-end CER 16.089 -> 13.161, line-matched 15.910 -> 12.290 (both clear the gate), and pages-cov CER 6.057 -> 6.064 (within the no-worse-by-0.05 gate). See docs/measurements/2026-09-23_line_fusion_fix.txt

the run floor for underline_strip, as a multiple of the page's median glyphish-component height h: a component narrower than this many h is never examined for rule stripping, and inside an examined component only a horizontal ink run at least this long is erased (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23, "Underlines are stripped from the pixels of over-wide components"). Derived, not guessed: `ocrcer-build aspect` (extended 2026-09-23) renders all 187 charset classes on all 32 shippable faces (`model/fonts.tsv`, the same 32-face convention `ocrcer-build metrics` uses, authored face included as face 0) at 256 px/em and reports, per class per face, the longest horizontal ink run divided by that face's x-height; the maximum over every class and face is the em dash on "OCRcer Technical Regular" (the authored face) at 340px run / 125.44px x-height = 2.7105 x-heights. lines.rule_run_heights is 2 x that maximum = 5.4209; the factor of 2 is authored headroom, same role as rule_aspect's clearance over its own measured bound, so that an em dash or a row of hyphens at a plausible page x-height sits well under the run floor and is never examined. See docs/measurements/2026-09-23_underline_strip.txt

the height, as a multiple of the page's median glyphish-component height h, above which a strip-produced piece is discarded as rule debris rather than kept as a component (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23, "Underline strip, second rule: straight bands only, keep crossing strokes, drop strip debris, and keep what was stripped"). Erasing a band out of an over-wide component can leave a tall/narrow remnant behind -- a box's vertical sides, once its top and bottom rules are gone -- that never existed as a component before the strip and is not glyph-shaped; this never touches an ordinary component that was never stripped. Derived, not guessed: the same 2026-09-23 `ocrcer-build aspect` run that derives lines.rule_run_heights also reports, per class per face, the tallest ink height divided by that face's x-height; the maximum over every class and face is the radical sign on "STIX Two Math Regular" at 304px height / 121.09px x-height = 2.5106 x-heights. lines.debris_heights is 2 x that maximum = 5.0211, the factor of 2 being the same authored headroom lines.rule_run_heights uses, so the tallest real letterform this engine's own bank can produce never qualifies as debris. See docs/measurements/2026-09-23_underline_strip.txt

rule 2, part 3b: a strip-produced piece whose width is <= 0.5 x h AND whose height exceeds this many h is dropped as debris even when it falls under lines.debris_heights (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23, "Two mechanisms named: the strip leaves a box-side sliver that merges lines"). Erasing a bordered numeric cell's top rule can leave the box's own left/right side behind as a narrow, tall sliver (observed 3x51px on filing__r000055/r000044) too narrow for lines.furniture_fraction and too short for lines.debris_heights (51px under a 65px floor), which survives as an ordinary component and seeds a wrong line-grouping band, fusing two real prose lines into one. The ink height is measured: the same 2026-09-23 `ocrcer-build aspect` run (extended) reports the tallest ink height, in x-heights, among classes whose own ink width is <= 0.5 x-height, over all 32 shippable faces; the maximum is `|` on "Fira Code Regular" at 316px height / 138.24px x-height = 2.2859 x-heights. The x1.5 factor over that measured height is a guess -- deliberately smaller than lines.rule_run_heights/lines.debris_heights's x2, because x2 would sit too close to the observed sliver (about 3.6-3.9 x h). See docs/measurements/2026-09-23_split_gate_and_strip_3b.txt

whether the rule-stripping pass runs: 0 leaves component labelling untouched, 1 erases straight rule bands inside over-wide components (rule 2 with part 3b) and re-labels. On since 2026-09-23 (ARCHITECTURE.md section 11, "Underline strip ships"): finfilings CER 16.932 -> 16.756, line-matched 16.843 -> 16.634; pages-cov unchanged at 6.089. See docs/measurements/2026-09-23_split_gate_and_strip_3b.txt

whether a narrow column fragment (a value box, a checkbox, a list marker) that shares a row with the first line of a wrapping left-column cell is joined there (0, today's behaviour), deferred past the cell's full wrapped text on overlap and pitch alone (1, `pair_cells`), deferred only when the wrap also passes the two extra tests in `lines.cell_wrap_slack`'s note (2), or (3) additionally requiring that a single-fragment row cannot vouch for a column on 40% overlap alone (it must not reach into a sibling fragment's own column) and that a vacuous extent -- the up/down scan never finding anything wider than the candidate's own right edge -- fails the fullness test closed rather than passing it by default. `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23 ("Worst pages, round 3" through "Cell pairing ships"): `filing__r000044`, `filing__r000396` and `filing__r000407` all showed the same mechanism -- `group_with_bands`'s row/fragment split correctly separates a genuine same-row column pair, but pairs it with whichever *other* fragment shares the row, which is wrong exactly when that row is only the first line of a wrapped multi-line cell. Level 1 measured a large finfilings win but failed pages-cov and mis-fired on `filing__r000407` itself. Level 2 added the fullness and own-row tests but regressed 35 CAD `drawing` pages and 2 invoices on pages-cov (an unsplit wide row overlapping every column above it, and the fullness test passing vacuously). Level 3 closes both: bench/pages-cov (625 pages) is bit-identical to control, CER 6.064% unchanged, 0 pages moved (the drawing-category no-regression gate holds exactly); finfilings (60 pages) improves end-to-end CER 13.161% -> 12.786% and line-matched CER 12.290% -> 11.686%. See docs/measurements/2026-09-23_cell_pairing.txt; not a threshold to sweep, a behaviour to switch

only read when `lines.cell_pairing >= 2`: a candidate continuation's *previous* left-column line must be "full" -- its right edge within this many x-heights of the left column's right extent in the contiguous block (the widest right edge among the block's own left-column lines, `pair_cells`'s `column_block_extent`) -- and the continuation line itself must carry no right-column fragment of its own row (already guaranteed by `pair_cells` only ever continuing through single-fragment rows). `docs/measurements/2026-09-23_cell_pairing.txt`: a wrapped line is full because it used the whole width its own block's other lines show is available; a short one-line label like "ii. LEI, if any" on `filing__r000407` never was, so it can no longer be mistaken for the first line of a wrap into the next unrelated label. Swept at 1.0/2.0/3.0 against the three named finfilings pages; 2.0 is where `filing__r000044`'s win holds and `filing__r000407` stays untouched. `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23 ("Cell pairing ships")

whether drop_checkboxes runs on the finished row/fragment groups: 0 leaves component labelling untouched, 1 drops a small, near-square, hollow rectangular outline -- a form checkbox -- and its contained mark before recognition (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23, "Checkboxes are furniture, not text"). Measured in `docs/measurements/2026-09-23_checkbox_truth_survey.md`: zero checkbox characters transcribed across 685 truth files (60 finfilings + 625 pages-cov), so any charset entry for a checkbox glyph can only ever be an insertion error; the fix is to drop the shape, the way lines.furniture_fraction and lines.rule_aspect drop other non-text ink. Ships 0 until measured against the pages-cov and finfilings gates in docs/measurements/2026-09-23_checkbox_drop.txt; not a threshold to sweep, a behaviour to switch

only read when lines.checkbox_drop is on: the lower size bound a checkbox candidate's longer side must clear, as a multiple of the line's own x-height. "Roughly x-height" per the direct pixel inspection of four checkbox-bearing finfilings pages in docs/measurements/2026-09-23_checkbox_truth_survey.md

only read when lines.checkbox_drop is on: the upper size bound a checkbox candidate's longer side must not exceed, as a multiple of the line's own cap-height. "About 1.6x cap height" per `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11, 2026-09-23 ("Checkboxes are furniture, not text")

only read when lines.checkbox_drop is on: how far from square a candidate's bounding box may be -- max(w,h)/min(w,h) must not exceed this -- before it looks like an ordinary letter rather than a checkbox. A form checkbox is drawn close to a perfect square; a capital O/0/D in this engine's own faces is reliably taller than it is wide, which is most of what keeps a lone letter from being read as an empty box

only read when lines.checkbox_drop is on: the most ink a checkbox candidate's own bounding box may hold, as a fraction of its area, before it is a solid mark rather than a hollow outline. A drawn box's ink is just its border ring, well under this fraction at ordinary stroke widths

only read when lines.checkbox_drop is on: how much of a checkbox candidate's own size a component fully contained inside it may occupy, as a fraction, before that content is ordinary glyph-sized text rather than a small checkbox mark. Above this fraction both the outline and its contents survive -- the test that lets a boxed 0/O/D stand, the false-positive case `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11 names explicitly

fewer gaps than this cannot show two populations, so the valley search has nothing to find. Swept over {2, 3, 4, 5} on two disjoint stride-13 samples of bench/pages and measured INERT: all four values return byte-identical CER, WER and F1 on both, because no line this corpus analyses has fewer than five gaps. So the sweep cannot choose this value and the provenance stays authored, on the argument in the first sentence, rather than being promoted to measured on a tie. Marked not tunable for the same reason: a sweep over it reports a winner that is only the first row

Otsu separability below this means one population, not two, and no valley is believed. Re-derived on bench/pages-cov once the fallback separated from the ceiling, because what this gate is worth depends entirely on where falling back lands: a demanding gate is unaffordable while falling back means using a ceiling as an estimate, and cheap once falling back means using the middle of the observed range. Swept as the cross product {0.65, 0.70, 0.75} ceiling x {0.35, 0.40, 0.45, 0.50} fallback x {0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90} separability, scored against ground-truth boxes over all 4205 lines of bench/pages-cov and confirmed on the disjoint 4205 lines of bench/holdout-cov. The quantity swept on is the share of adjacent-glyph gaps classified wrongly, which isolates this rule from component merging on purpose; the end-to-end consequence is reported separately. At the chosen ceiling and fallback, 0.80 measures 1.556% of gaps wrong on bench/pages-cov and 1.587% on the holdout, against 1.902% and 2.001% for the superseded 0.6 with a shared 0.7 fallback. The 2026-09-21 finding that 0.9 fell off a cliff was a property of that shared fallback and does not transfer. Superseded on 2026-09-22: 0.80 is the argmax of the gap-error metric and 0.70 is the argmax end to end, and where those two disagree the end-to-end figure decides. 0.70 beats 0.80 on every one of ten paired comparisons across two disjoint 48/49-page samples, and beats 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6 on both; on all 625 pages of bench/pages-cov, same model file and same binary, 0.70 measures CER 6.554% WER 27.478% F1 76.206% against 0.80's 6.651%, 28.233% and 75.973%. The gap-error metric scores every adjacent-glyph gap alike, so it cannot see that a gate which merges two words costs two tokens while one that splits one word costs one -- which is the whole of the 1.02-point precision gain

the ceiling on a valley the line's own gaps produced, and nothing else: no valley may sit where a gap this wide is called intra-word. Unchanged in value; what changed on 2026-09-22 is that it no longer doubles as the fallback, which is words.no_valley_x_heights. The 2026-09-21 sweep that chose 0.7 over the authored 1.0 was run with the two roles sharing this number, so its margin was partly the fallback's and its end-to-end figures came from the two-valued bench/pages; the value survives re-derivation on bench/pages-cov as the ceiling alone, where 0.65, 0.70 and 0.75 measure 1.576%, 1.556% and 1.643% of gaps wrong on the train corpus and 1.525%, 1.587% and 1.633% on the holdout. 0.70 is kept: it is the argmax on neither corpus by more than six hundredths of a point and is the best of the three by perfectly split lines on both

the threshold for a line whose gaps produced no believable valley -- too few of them, or too little separation. Separated from lone_gap_x_heights on 2026-09-22 because the two answer different questions: a ceiling can afford to be generous since a measured valley usually decides, whereas a fallback IS the decision and must sit where such boundaries are observed to sit. Measured, not guessed: over the 625 pages of bench/pages-cov the best-possible single threshold for a page has a median of 0.406, 0.415, 0.444, 0.429 and 0.466 x-heights at 14, 18, 21, 28 and 40 px/em, and the 0.7 ceiling is ABOVE that best-possible threshold on 64.8%, 69.6%, 78.4%, 86.4% and 88.8% of pages at those sizes -- which is the mechanism behind the deleted spaces this change exists to fix. 0.40 is the low end of that median band, chosen over 0.45 because it is better on the holdout by perfectly split lines (78.19% against 77.81%) at the same gap-error rate within four hundredths of a point

the narrowest gap a believed valley may call a word space, as a fraction of the x-height; 0 removes the floor. The mirror of lone_gap_x_heights' ceiling: that one says no valley may sit where a gap this WIDE is called intra-word, this one says no valley may call a gap this NARROW a space. It floors the narrowest called space, not the threshold -- the threshold is the widest intra-word gap and is small on any well-set line. Without it a valley search given only intra-word gaps still finds a valley among them and Otsu separability on 1,1,3,1,2 px believes it, so a single-word segment splits into its letters -- never a problem while lines ran the width of the page, and immediate once lines.column_gap_heights cuts a line into single-word segments: bench/pages-cov invoice at 18px read Unit as `U n i t` and 112.50 as `112 .50`. Swept over {0, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6} on 90 pages of bench/pages-cov (stride 7, coprime with the 5-size ladder) at two settings of lines.column_gap_heights, and 0.3 is the argmax of word F1 at both: cut off 77.503% against 76.660% at 0.4, cut at 2.5 75.440% against 74.839%, and it is also the CER minimum with the cut on (8.569%). Inert at 0.15 and 0.2 with the cut off, to the digit. no_valley_x_heights (0.4) is the ceiling on this value rather than a target for it -- above equality the rule contradicts itself, rejecting a valley for calling a gap a space and then falling back to a rule that calls the same gap a space -- and the measurement landed below it. The conversion truncates, so the value selects an integer pixel floor and is coarse where it matters: on a 9 px x-height 0.23 to 0.33 is a 2 px floor and 0.34 to 0.44 is a 3 px floor, so 0.3 rejects 112.50 and Amount but still splits 3.75 and Unit, which 0.4 catches and pays for elsewhere

fewest member boxes a fragment needs before the fixed-pitch test (ARCHITECTURE.md section 11) runs at all; a plausible starting value, not a sweep. 0 disables the test outright and must reproduce the prior gap-valley-only behaviour byte for byte -- the control the 2026-09-22 fixed-pitch measurement checks
the fraction of a fragment's centre-to-centre distances that must sit on an integer multiple of the median pitch before the fragment is called fixed-pitch; a plausible starting value, not a sweep
how far a centre-to-centre distance may sit from an integer multiple of the median pitch and still count as agreeing, as a fraction of that median; a plausible starting value, not a sweep

diagnostic ablation switch for the 2026-09-22 amendment (ARCHITECTURE.md section 11): 0 skips merging x-overlapping members into one cell before centre distances are taken, testing raw member boxes instead -- the pre-amendment behaviour. Not a threshold to sweep; both toggles at 1 must reproduce the amended build byte for byte, the control docs/measurements/2026-09-22_fixed_pitch_spaces.txt's amendment ablation checks

the third amendment's fitted-grid residual test (ARCHITECTURE.md section 11, 'the grid vote failed too'): fits a straight line through the fragment's cell positions instead of voting on pairwise distances. Bounded fallback applied 2026-09-22: measured proportional false positives 2.48% at cg=0 against a required <=0.5%, statement F1 67.204%/deletions 333 against a required >=68.278%/<=296, ACCOUNT STATEMENT fused at 37 of 55 font/size pairs (was 4 of 55). Default reverts to 0 (cell merge, vote/fitted-grid off, the 'merge only' row: mono recall 94.8%, prop FP 1.62%) per the amendment's own pre-decided fallback. 1 still exercises the fitted-grid test for diagnostic comparison; not a threshold to sweep. docs/measurements/2026-09-22_fixed_pitch_spaces.txt, section 'Fitted grid'
three atoms is enough for a broken glyph and for an accented letter; more is a cost with no case behind it
a merged candidate wider than this is two characters, not one broken one

below this width (in x-heights) an atom is not searched for interior cuts. Swept 2026-09-23 (ARCHITECTURE.md section 11, "split gate"): 1.15 missed the 11 px `0$` atom at h=10; 1.0 helped finfilings but cost pages-cov +0.203 CER; 1.09 improves both (pages-cov 6.127->6.089, finfilings 17.064->16.932). docs/measurements/2026-09-23_split_gate_and_strip_3b.txt
how many interior cuts one component may be offered
a column profile minimum this far below the local mean is a candidate cut
a piece narrower than this is a stroke, not a character

how much of the narrower component's own width two adjacent components' column overlap must cover before atoms() glues them into one atom; either fully inside the other's column range always merges (i/j dots, `:`/`;`, `=`). 0 is the legacy any-overlap rule.
